It further identifies evidence preservation and structured answer construction as key considerations for reliable RAG. This work provides a reproducible framework for investigating retrieval effectiveness and evidence-grounded generation.
Information Retrieval.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 8 tables. TREC 2026 RAG Track. Code: https://github.com/Elyasirankhah/TREC-RAG-2026

Information Retrieval.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team's channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. We evaluate Memanto, a memory agent that ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench, which tests memory through 600 simulated workplace tasks, each validated as requiring memory. Running in the Hermes agent harness with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations per conversation, Memanto completes 503 tasks (83.83%). The strongest configuration reported by the benchmark's authors, Mem0 with GPT-5.6-Luna and up to 60 iterations, completes 424 (70.67%). Memanto's run also has the lowest total cost ($10.86, against $61.48 for the cheapest reported run) and the shortest median task latency (15.32s). Grading uses the benchmark's own judge, but the agent model differs, so these results compare complete systems. The memory system affects both whether an agent completes such tasks and what completion costs.
Information Retrieval.comment: Future version will submit to ACL

Information Retrieval.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

Information Retrieval.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
Information Retrieval.summary:
Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones.
  On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.
Information Retrieval.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, including appendices. Evaluations on WDC Products and STaRK-Amazon

Information Retrieval.title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
Information Retrieval.summary: Text encoders turn earnings calls into vectors for search, for language models that answer from retrieved passages, and for forecasting models. A live retriever can use an encoder trained once on all available text, as finance retrievers are, but a backtest needs an encoder that read no text written after the date of each vector. To address this look-ahead bias, from 412,248 calls we train vintages under four pretraining recipes, with yearly cutoffs from 2010 to 2024, and each vintage reads only text dated on or before its cutoff. We then fine-tune each vintage on the question-answer pairs of the calls themselves. The vintages we train on calls alone, with 33.8M parameters, retrieve answers on held-out calls better than the general retrievers we tested in every test quarter. Their vectors also raise by about half the rank correlation between next-day returns and forecasts built from past returns and firm size. When each vintage continues the previous one, a later vintage retrieves better on earlier quarters than the vintage available at the time, and a point-in-time language model that answers from the passages the later vintage retrieves inherits the gain. The 2024 vintage of our families also forecasts earnings surprises better, although the interval of this gain includes zero on calls that no vintage read. It forecasts returns no better, so point-in-time vintages matter most for retrieval and little for forecasts of returns.
Information Retrieval.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the 3rd IEEE International Workshop on Large Language Models for Finance, IEEE BigData 2026. Code: https://github.com/Alessiobrini/point-in-time-encoders-for-earnings-calls

Information Retrieval.title: Pre-Crawl Prioritization and Seed Classification for Large-Scale Web Archiving
Information Retrieval.summary: Pre-crawl prioritization systems decide which pages to fetch first before indexing, aiming to improve crawl efficiency and coverage. Existing approaches based on page popularity and relevance are unsuited to web-archival crawlers that prioritize comprehensive coverage over selective retrieval. We explore prioritization techniques tailored to web archival operations using URL lexical analysis, dynamic domain reputation systems, and HTTP response analysis to inform crawl scheduling decisions. By incorporating predictive models that estimate content change and disappearance probabilities, we improve crawl completeness while reducing redundant visits to stable resources. Through large-scale experiments, we demonstrate that our methods improve archival effectiveness and resource utilization compared to undirected crawling.
Information Retrieval.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Published in the 2025 ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries (JCDL)

Information Retrieval.title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: AI agents that talk with users across many sessions need long-term memory to stay coherent and personalized. Existing approaches use either flat retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that ignores how memories connect, or entity-centric knowledge graphs. Entity-centric graphs split each message into separate triples, which loses its context, and in conversations the speakers become hubs linked to almost every message, so propagation through them tells retrieval little. We present GAAMA, a graph-augmented associative memory that organizes conversations around topics. It keeps verbatim episodes, uses an LLM to distill them into atomic facts and topic concepts, and then synthesizes higher-order reflections. These four node types are linked by five kinds of structural edges, and topic concepts supply the cross-cutting paths, so mega-hubs do not form. Retrieval blends nearest-neighbor similarity search with Personalized PageRank whose transitions depend on edge type. We also introduce GRAFT (Graph Repair by Augmenting Facts & Topology), an offline repair step: for questions whose retrieved evidence fell short, a bounded ReAct agent searches memory again and records the grounded answer as a fresh fact, so later questions find it directly without extra query-time cost. On LoCoMo10, GAAMA achieves the highest average score of all compared methods (79.1%) and is competitive in every question category; GRAFT adds a small further gain. In a controlled comparison, replacing GAAMA's concept-linked facts with entity relation triples lowers reward by 3.0 pp. On MemoryArena, scored on what memory alone determines, GAAMA has the best score on average.

Information Retrieval.title: CogRec: Structure-Cognitive Fast-and-Slow Reasoning for Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative recommendation reformulates next-item prediction as identifier sequence generation, yet existing methods mainly treat the generated identifiers as target sequences to be memorized, leaving their hierarchical and relational structure underused for explicit reasoning. We propose CogRec, a structure-cognitive fast-and-slow reasoning framework that grounds intermediate reasoning in the same SID topology used for target generation. CogRec augments the vertical SID hierarchy with intra-layer semantic graphs and introduces SID Routing to represent recommendation reasoning through layer-wise Match, LateralJump, and Explore operations. These operations provide a structural interpretation of fast localization and slow navigation. A supervised multi-stage pipeline aligns newly introduced SID tokens, establishes direct generation, and trains natural-language and SID Routing branches from a shared checkpoint. Experiments on three Amazon Reviews 2014 categories show dataset-dependent effects of SID Routing. Routing improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 over its direct-generation counterpart on Beauty and Sports, while reducing both metrics on Toys. These results characterize the benefits and dataset-dependent behavior of SID-grounded intermediate reasoning for generative recommendation. Code is available at https://github.com/caskcsg/CogRec.

Information Retrieval.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
Information Retrieval.summary: Learning effective feature interactions is essential for industrial recommender systems. DCN and DCNv2 efficiently automate polynomial feature crossing. However, their cross layers construct interactions using only non-negative integer powers of the input features, with the maximum degree controlled by network depth. Consequently, they cannot directly represent the reciprocal terms required for ratios, rates, and normalized counts unless such features are explicitly provided as inputs. We introduce DCDN, a Deep Cross-Division Network that augments a DCNv2-style cross layer with a division branch. DCDN jointly learns product, ratio, and mixed product-ratio interactions. We characterize the representable interactions as multivariate Laurent polynomials and show that a $K$-layer DCDN generates Laurent monomials of $\ell_1$-order up to $K+1$, with signed degree between $-K$ and $K+1$. We evaluate DCDN against a production-optimized neural-ranking baseline built around DCNv2 and supplied with manually engineered ratio features. Replacing the DCNv2 block with DCDN allowed us to eliminate the entire class of manually engineered ratio features from the model input, reducing the number of input features by $40.1\%$. DCDN is deployed in the production ranking stack of a major short-video service. In a live A/B test on this service, DCDN increased likes by $3.25\%$, shares by $16.26\%$, total view time (TVT) by $0.33\%$, and clicks to open fullscreen by $0.38\%$; all changes were statistically significant. The number of shown videos decreased slightly ($-0.24\%$). These results demonstrate that DCDN can improve user engagement while eliminating reliance on manually engineered ratio features. Our code is publicly released at https://github.com/rw404/DCDN.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted at WSDM 2027. 14 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables

Information Retrieval.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wrocław, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the best of thirteen backbones from seven pretraining paradigms reaches 94.7%. Accuracy falls slowly as candidates are added: for DINOv2, by about 0.8 points each time their number doubles. A natural design for a phone guide compares a photograph only with statues near the user. In simulation this helps, but less than an equal number of randomly chosen statues does, so random subsampling overstates its value; a permutation test ties the penalty to the real layout (p = 0.005). Used as a weight instead of a filter, location raises DINOv2 from 93.4% to 98.7% for a simulated user 25 m from the statue. With the query's photographer withheld, learned local-feature matching raises DINOv2 accuracy from 81.8% to 85.5% and also improves DINOv3. Comparing the two best candidates cuts DINOv2's false acceptance of unknown statues from 38.3% to 19.6% at 90% known acceptance.
Information Retrieval.comment: 23 pages, 6 figures in the main text; includes appendix. Project page: https://turhancan97.github.io/doppeldwarf-306/

Information Retrieval.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
Information Retrieval.summary: Long-term memory is essential for personalized agentic systems that interact with users over long time periods, yet current architectures only capture what happened while leaving the reasoning of why it happened to be derived later by underlying LLMs. These events can, however, convey not only what a user experienced but also how that experience shaped their behavioral patterns. We introduce STARK, a dual-graph memory architecture which treats these events not just as nodes but also as edges between behavioral insights. STARK maintains an Episodic Graph which records interactions as temporally, causally, and semantically linked episodes; and an Insight Graph which represents LLM-extracted behavioral signals scored by how many events support them, connected by the very events that led to them. At inference, behavioral knowledge is retrieved directly from insight nodes grounded by event-as-edges, eliminating repeated episodic traversal. The event-as-edge structure also naturally enables projecting the knowledge graph into a relational embedding space where cross-user transfer becomes possible under shared contextual circumstances, allowing the system to infer missing insights for cold-start users. Evaluations show that STARK improves by 1.48 judge score on LongMemEval information extraction and 0.93 on LoCoMo open domain questions over state of the art. On the public LongLaMP abstract-generation benchmark, cross-user transfer improves open-ended judge scores by 0.7 points and ROUGE-L by 3 at 5% graph sparsity.

Information Retrieval.title: From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search
Information Retrieval.summary: Agentic search demands that a search engine move beyond per document relevance ranking to assemble document sets optimized for downstream LLM reasoning. Prior work addresses this either by improving individual pipeline stages in isolation or by applying RL based selection on top of relevance trained upstream modules, leaving the full stack unaligned to utility for reasoning. We propose rubric aligned search, a framework that unifies the traditional search pipeline under a single supervision surface. For each query, we derive a rubric from coarse to fine, specifying weighted positive criteria that the document set must satisfy and negative criteria that it must avoid. From this rubric we derive two training signals. First, a lightweight labeler distills rubric grounded judgments into per document utility labels, which supervise a contrastive dual encoder for retrieval and a multi task ranker trained with four rubric aligned scoring heads. Second, a rubric conditioned evaluator produces a set level reward that drives a dual branch RL selector, combining GRPO with best rollout distillation to resolve credit assignment in subset optimization. Deployed in Yuanbao Search, the pipeline improves end to end answer quality by 8.52% over the online production baseline.
Information Retrieval.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables, accepted at KDD 2027

Information Retrieval.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
Information Retrieval.summary: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. On the three long-form tasks of LongLaMP with three LLMs, SP-Refine outperforms LongLaMP's retrieval-augmented baseline in 25 of 27 ROUGE and METEOR comparisons, by 10.2% on average and by up to 35.8%. Annotating users' own texts with the extracted profiles shows that StylePrism captures concrete, checkable habits, from the order of rhetorical moves to a reviewer's sign-off. Ablations show that the profile helps as revision guidance, not as a replacement for the samples: writing from the profile alone is worse in all 27 comparisons, while a single implicit-inference call is a cheaper alternative that comes close. Oracle variants that let the reviser see the reference, together with reference-free controls, show that larger refinement gains require information unavailable at inference time.

Information Retrieval.title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems
Information Retrieval.summary: Large-scale recommendation systems face "Memory Wall" bottlenecks due to massive, dense embedding tables. While generative retrieval uses discrete tokens for IDs, high-dimensional context still relies on inefficient dense formats. Inspired by computer vision data compression, we propose Dual-purpose Semantic IDs to achieve LLM-level I/O efficiency. Our methodology uses hierarchical quantization to condense continuous embeddings into discrete Semantic IDs performing two concurrent roles: (1) Collaborative Identity: modeling user-item interactions via learnable embedding table; and (2) Content Reconstruction: using a lightweight Semantic Decoder for on-the-fly embedding approximation. This approach replaces massive vector storage with on-demand reconstruction, reducing system overhead and data footprints. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework through offline evaluations and successful online deployment in production-scale ranking and retrieval systems at a major video sharing platform, showing that discrete tokens are indeed all you need for highly efficient, content-rich recommendation.

Information Retrieval.title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing
Information Retrieval.summary:
Online A/B testing is the standard approach for evaluating changes to user-facing systems, such as a new recommendation or ranking policy, before deployment. While the difference-in-means estimator of a standard A/B test is unbiased, it often suffers from high variance. When the treatment and production policies choose the same actions with similar probabilities, the resulting observations can add noise while providing little information about the difference between the policies. Consequently, A/B tests can require large amounts of traffic and long durations to detect small treatment effects. Existing variance-reduction methods mainly improve the estimator after the data-collection scheme has been fixed, and recent overlap-aware designs only optimize a single traffic split between the two policies; thereby, they cannot direct traffic to the actions on which the policies disagree.
  In this paper, we jointly optimize how actions are sampled and how the resulting observations are used to estimate the treatment effect. Our contributions are two-fold. First, building on pairwise off-policy evaluation, we derive the variance-optimal action-level logging policy for estimating the average treatment effect between two policies, which has a closed-form solution for any fixed control variate. Second, we use historical logs to jointly optimize the logging policy and a control variate to further reduce variance. Our experimental results in simulated policy A/B tests show that our designs estimate the average treatment effect more accurately than existing variance reduction methods on every evaluated setting, while generally improving statistical power and reducing how often the worse policy is selected. As a result, our designs enable practitioners to reach reliable deployment decisions with considerably less online traffic.

Information Retrieval.title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
Information Retrieval.summary: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user-item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.

Information Retrieval.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewrites advantages using a deduplicated group reward and marginal advantage within GRPO, avoiding auxiliary diversity objectives. Deployed online with a lightweight 0.1B backbone, TS-GEAR serves over 150 million queries per day in the search advertising pipeline of Taobao Shangou, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods on both HitRate and geographic validity, and achieving 3.8% gains in ad impressions and 4.2% in ad revenue.

Information Retrieval.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
Information Retrieval.summary: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. We study the leader finding problem, where the query is a project and a team and the output is a ranked list of candidate leaders. We model the problem in a probabilistic framework that combines technical fit, managerial knowledge, and communication with the team, and we propose one evaluation metric for each of these qualities. On two large collections built from Stack Overflow, the best configuration of our model more than doubles the NDCG@10 of the strongest baseline. These results show that a ranking of leaders must balance several qualities that topical expertise alone does not capture.
Information Retrieval.comment: Extended version of the ICTIR '21 short paper (doi:10.1145/3471158.3472230). 30 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables

Information Retrieval.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. Moving queries to a different encoder normally requires re-embedding the whole corpus, and at cold start there are no query logs while every document embedded by the new encoder incurs an API or compute cost. We present ERA (Embed, Route, Adapt), a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval. ERA spends a small anchor budget on maximally informative documents, selected from the existing target index via Cosine Farthest Point Sampling, trains a lightweight adapter with a Manifold Alignment Loss that couples directional alignment with orthogonal regularization to prevent representation collapse, and pairs the adapter with a deterministic router that escalates the rare, hard queries that define perceived retrieval quality. Across five BEIR datasets, ERA matches or outperforms point-wise L2 and embedding-conversion baselines, with relative gains of up to 35% nDCG@10 on Arguana, and on clustered corpora its anchor selection also improves prior methods under a fixed anchor budget. With 1.2 ms of adapter and router overhead on top of a ~20 ms local encoder, ERA at a 20% nominal escalation budget reduces end-to-end query latency from roughly 160 ms to 38-86 ms while concentrating escalations on the queries where the projection fails most.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
Proof-assistant kernels with strict propositions---Lean 4, Agda's Prop, and Coq/Rocq's SProp---build proof irrelevance into conversion ($p \equiv q$ for $p, q : P$), equating all derivations of a theorem. While natural for pure mathematics, judgmental proof irrelevance breaks provenance in verified scientific stores, where predicates, refinements, and institutional maps must distinguish independent derivations for consilience and counterfactual retraction; with subsingleton elimination, it also breaks normalization and algorithmic transitivity.
  We present the type-theoretic and institutional foundations of Eigenius, a kernel for provenance-preserving scientific stores. First, we formulate a dependent kernel with cumulative universes (Prop, Set, $\mathsf{Type}_k$ for $k \ge 1$), impredicative Prop, inductive families with index-forced subsingleton elimination, and intensional identity types: conversion $\equiv$ is untyped orthogonal-CRS joinability, while proof irrelevance is a witnessed axiom ($\mathsf{irrel} : ΠP:\mathsf{Prop}.\,Πp,q:P.\,\mathsf{Id}\,P\,p\,q$). Second, coercion-free subsumption unifies cumulativity, $Π$-covariant subtyping, and ontology inclusions; its bidirectional fragments ($\mathcal{K}_0, \mathcal{K}_1$) satisfy subject reduction, match declarative typing, and compile to heuristic-free checkers ($\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1$) sound and complete relative to strong normalization. Third, we link external verifiers via constructive institutions (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), internalize justification logic with Why-provenance $\mathsf{supp}(j,P)$, and type open-world knowledge graphs via TTR. Finally, we prove consistency in Grothendieck universes and mechanize the metatheory in Lean 4 with zero sorry.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Guard Analysis and Safe Erasure Gradual Typing: a Type System for Elixir
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
We formalize a new type system for Elixir, a dynamically typed functional programming language of growing popularity that runs on the Erlang virtual machine. Our system combines gradual typing with semantic subtyping to enable precise, sound, and practical static type analysis, without requiring any changes to Elixir's compilation pipeline or runtime. Type soundness is ensured by leveraging runtime checks -- both implicit, from the Erlang VM, and explicit, via developer-written guards.
  Central to our approach are two key innovations: the notion of "strong functions", which can be assigned precise types even when applied to inputs that may fall outside their intended domain; and a fine-grained analysis of guards that enables accurate type refinement for case expressions and guarded function definitions. While type information is erased before execution and not used by the compiler, our "safe erasure" gradual typing strategy maintains soundness and expressiveness without compromising compatibility or performance. This work lays the theoretical foundation for Elixir's new type system, outlines its integration into recent versions of the language, and demonstrates its effectiveness on large-scale industrial codebases.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Characterization and Decidability of FC-Definable Regular Languages
Logic in Computer Science.summary: FC is a first-order logic that reasons over all factors of a finite word using concatenation, and can define non-regular languages like that of all squares (ww). In this paper, we establish that there are regular languages that are not FC-definable. Moreover, we give a decidable characterization of the FC-definable regular languages in terms of algebra, automata, and regular expressions. The latter of which is natural and concise: Star-free generalized regular expressions extended with the Kleene star of terminal words.

Logic in Computer Science.title: QANAD: A Model-Driven Framework for Quantitative Analysis and Synthesis of Activity Diagrams via Probabilistic Model Checking
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Probabilistic model checking is a widely used formal verification technique to automatically verify qualitative and quantitative QoS properties for probabilistic models, such as reliability, performance, and cost. However, devising suitable and representative models for systems of interest in model checkers, writing corresponding properties, and verifying them requires domain knowledge in probabilistic models, formal verification, and the target model checkers. This unavoidably makes model checking not easily accessible for researchers and engineers who may lack the required knowledge. Previous work has extended UML activity diagrams with probability and time, along with quality annotations, developed transformations from activity diagrams to probabilistic models which model checkers support, and implemented accompanying tools for automation. The research, however, is fragmented, informal, or not fully open, making its use, extension, and adaptation non-trivial. To mitigate these challenges, we introduce QANAD, a comprehensive verification framework for activity diagrams, that includes a new profile for probability, time, parameters, and quality annotations, a semantics interpretation of activity diagrams in Markov models variants (DTMCs, MDPs, and CTMCs) and their parametric versions, and a set of formal transformation rules from activity diagrams to the PRISM modelling language, supported by the leading model checkers PRISM and Storm. The theory underpinning QANAD has been realised into transformation implementation using model-driven engineering, enabling fully automated model transformation with automated verification using (parametric) probabilistic model checking and semi-automated synthesis. We demonstrate QANAD on a case study where multiple robots are used for delivery in a hospital environment and evaluated six other examples from the literature.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Accepted version by the journal of Software and Systems Modeling (SoSyM)

Logic in Computer Science.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. Yet an LLM is a general-purpose text generator, whereas a formula in a fixed formal language fragment follows a well-defined syntax. We therefore ask whether text generation is needed at all. For the formal language of linear temporal logic (LTL), we show that this translation can instead be broken down into answering a set of questions with pre-defined answers. We then construct a System-One model, a recent class of NL-based classifier, to provide such answers and enable us to translate a natural language instruction into an LTL instruction. On three benchmarks, our translator matches or exceeds the accuracy of the best local LLMs available, at up to one order of magnitude lower runtime and energy consumption. We show that it generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 24 pages, 5 figures

Logic in Computer Science.title: Bounded Treewidth Rulesets Are Not Finitely Controllable
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
An ontology language $O$ is finitely controllable with respect to a query language $Q$ if the finite and unrestricted variants of the query entailment problem for $\langle O, Q\rangle$ coincide. In this paper, we study finite controllability (FC) in its classical sense for existential rules, where $O$ is a class of existential rules and $Q$ is the class of all Boolean conjunctive queries (BCQs).
  A natural question in this line of work is whether the class of bounded treewidth sets (BTS) is finitely controllable with respect to BCQs. We answer this question negatively: we exhibit a simple set of rules over a binary signature and prove that it is BTS but not FC. Moreover, using the same set of rules, we show that two subclasses of BTS, namely GBTS and pieceful, are not FC either.

Logic in Computer Science.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
Expecting guardrails to provide a general guarantee of safety fails to recognize the limits of computational enforcement and policy specification. We argue that promising such perfection is an ethical failure of precision, and that invoking it to abdicate responsibility is a moral failure. Guardrails can support responsible action, but cannot relieve researchers, developers, policymakers, or users of their obligations to examine what they claim, permit, and prevent.
  We establish a precise computational boundary. If every finite string is a possible output of a language model, a computable guard that blocks every forbidden output and passes every permitted one exists if and only if the policy is decidable. For an undecidable policy, every guard misclassifies infinitely many strings, and every guard that blocks all forbidden outputs excludes infinitely many permitted ones. We apply this characterization to arithmetic truth, program behavior, and harmful instructions to an idealized recipient. We distinguish guards from execution monitors, identify bounded and interceptable cases admitting exact enforcement, and explain why the results establish no positive lower bound on average error.
  Exact enforcement does not establish that a policy adequately captures safety. Conservative exclusion may withhold warnings, remedies, or challenges needed to recognize the policy's own defects. Human oversight cannot substitute for judgment: an apparent controller can become an instrument of purposes they have ceased to examine. Responsible governance requires continued critical challenge and the intellectual and moral humility to recognize possible flaws in our machines, rules, policies, and ourselves. The impossibility of a general assurance of perfection is a condition responsible practice must confront, not a responsibility that another guardrail - or another guard - can remove.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 31 pages, including a one-page executive summary and a self-contained proof appendix. Sustainable Systems Laboratory Technical Report SSL-TR-2026-002, Preprint v0.1

Logic in Computer Science.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story.
  During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve.
  We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities.
  But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accumulates semantic debt: definitions and results with unchecked mathematical interpretations are reused as foundations for further work. A library may keep compiling and produce the desired formal theorem while users lose track of which mathematical claims they can responsibly rely on.
  Reliable reuse is also a prerequisite for Terence Tao's vision of formal mathematics as something people can navigate, explain, learn from, and build with. This paper takes our work connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture as a case study of the challenges of reliable reuse as formal developments scale.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 7 pages, 0 figures. A case study in Lean formalization, semantic trust, and repository versioning

Social and Information Networks.title: Growing Hypergraphs with Homophily
Social and Information Networks.summary: There are many extant models of hypergraphs with interactions governed by attribute-based homophily between nodes, but most assume independence between edges conditional on node parameters. Relaxing this assumption, we study a mechanistic model of growing hypergraphs in which edge formation is influenced by both previous edges and binary node labels. Edges form in this model as noisy copies of previous edges, where the transmission of nodes from one edge to the next depends on multiple homophilic mechanisms between labels. These homophilic mechanisms give rise to tunable assortative structure in the hypergraph. We derive a power law for the degree distribution in this model and describe the long-term dynamics of the joint distribution of labels contained in edges. Our model defines a likelihood over a labeled hypergraph, allowing us to use standard maximum-likelihood techniques to structure algorithms. We estimate the model parameters on synthetic and real data via (stochastic) expectation maximization. These estimates give statistically-principled descriptions of the operation of homophily in empirical polyadic systems. We also demonstrate an approach to community detection via simulated annealing which, though computationally expensive, achieves competitive results on both synthetic data and certain empirical data sets known to be challenging to community detection techniques based on the edge-independence assumption. Our findings highlight the benefits of incorporating edge- and label-dependence in higher-order modeling and data analysis, and point to several directions for future work.

Social and Information Networks.title: The Times They Are A-Changin': Tracking Global Trends through the Lens of Web Search
Social and Information Networks.summary: Human societies have always left traces of their collective priorities, from cave drawings and stone carvings to chronicles on papyrus and printed books. In the digital era, these traces increasingly emerge through social media footprints and web search behavior at a global scale. We construct the first large-scale longitudinal dataset of Google Year in Search trends, spanning 15 years, to characterize how collective public attention evolves across countries and time. Because search engines like Google and Bing do not publicly release raw search logs, Year in Search provides a rare cross-national archive of annually salient search interests. The dataset is supplemented with a manually curated, unified ten-category semantic taxonomy with strong inter-annotator agreement. We focus on four categories (Information Seeking, Personality, Entertainment, and Sports) to investigate how collective attention varies across geographic and socio-cultural contexts. Our analyses reveal a consistently glocalized structure of collective attention: countries converge strongly in profession-level personality attention while remaining differentiated in the specific individuals they search for, yet profession-level similarity is only weakly associated with geographic region and income group. Information seeking is globally dominated by politics and health, while regional distributions show varying degrees of divergence. Crisis periods are associated with both shared and regionally differentiated shifts. Entertainment and sports attention likewise combine globally prominent interests with regional differentiation. Overall, our findings suggest that web search data provide a valuable computational lens for observing collective attention at scale, acting as a living archive of how societal priorities vary across countries and change over time.
Social and Information Networks.comment: This paper has been accepted at the 21st International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2027)

Social and Information Networks.title: How coalition size shapes bill cosponsorship in the U.S. Congress
Social and Information Networks.summary: Legislation is built by coalitions, yet studied through pairwise ties. Using five decades of U.S. House and Senate cosponsorship (1973-2025), we represent each bill as a group. Prior ties to current members predict who joins better than ties to the sponsor, and group history (earlier co-appearance with pairs of those members) produces a larger likelihood gain than sponsor ties alone. Coalition formation therefore retains a social memory of earlier groups: cooperation is organized around relational histories embedded in the coalition already assembled, which sponsor-cosponsor ties alone cannot recover. Completed coalitions also recur and share subgroups more often than degree- and size-preserving nulls predict. Party sorting peaks in coalitions of a few dozen members; as Congress polarized, small coalitions retained their cross-party share while mid-size coalitions became more partisan. Women are over-represented chiefly in coalitions led by Democratic women, although same-gender sponsor matching is close to zero after adjustment.
Social and Information Networks.comment: 43 pages, 22 figures

Social and Information Networks.title: Convergence and acceleration of a nonlinear fixed-point iteration for computing the Fitness Centrality of general graphs
Social and Information Networks.summary: We establish the global convergence of the (non-homogeneous) Fitness Centrality algorithm for general graphs, deriving an explicit convergence bound for the corresponding fixed-point iteration. From the computational point of view, we show how the convergence can be dramatically improved by Anderson acceleration and by switching to Newton's method once a sufficiently good approximation to the fixed point has been found. The efficacy of this strategy is illustrated by numerical experiments on different types of graphs.
Social and Information Networks.comment: 29 pages, 3 figures

Social and Information Networks.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
Social and Information Networks.summary: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. We study the leader finding problem, where the query is a project and a team and the output is a ranked list of candidate leaders. We model the problem in a probabilistic framework that combines technical fit, managerial knowledge, and communication with the team, and we propose one evaluation metric for each of these qualities. On two large collections built from Stack Overflow, the best configuration of our model more than doubles the NDCG@10 of the strongest baseline. These results show that a ranking of leaders must balance several qualities that topical expertise alone does not capture.
Social and Information Networks.comment: Extended version of the ICTIR '21 short paper (doi:10.1145/3471158.3472230). 30 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables

Artificial Intelligence.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
Artificial Intelligence.summary: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
Artificial Intelligence.summary:
AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results show attacks transferring to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor. Our results suggest that monitor evasion evaluations can easily mislead: an evaluation using only basic attack methods may give false confidence that a monitor is strong.
  The sensitivity to attack-policy choice raises a problem: interpreting any particular result as evidence about deployment performance requires justification. The transcripts produced by attack policies are proxies for the dangerous behaviour a monitor must flag in deployment. These proxies can introduce visible artefacts, such as reasoning about a ``side task'' absent from the instructions shown to the monitor, that affect monitor judgements. Given the sensitivity above, the choice of proxy can change an evaluation's conclusion. Reading these results as evidence about deployment therefore requires a separate legitimacy argument for why the proxies are informative, including any justification of conservativeness. Making convincing arguments remains an open problem.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of generated traces. Its estimated generation cost per recovered problem is nearly identical, while its cost per accepted trace is 30% lower. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on traces mined by DART achieves the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. These results demonstrate that revisiting rejected traces with DART can expand problem coverage and provide effective post-training data.

Artificial Intelligence.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across 20 domains, 100 scenarios vary group size, acoustics, and follow-up demands to form 800 cases (408 tool-augmented, 392 tool-free). Joint Task Success (JTS) requires all user goals, privacy boundaries, and terminal states to hold jointly, while Pure JTS further disallows unauthorized tool calls; Attribution, Threading, and Coordination (ATC) diagnostics localize failures. Across 13 voice agents, proprietary systems peak at 62.24\% tool-free and 65.44\% tool-augmented success, while open-weight models remain below 20\%. ATC diagnostics show that open-weight models lag primarily in multi-turn attribution and threading, and controlled contrasts reveal that larger groups consistently degrade joint task success across capable systems. By coupling reactive multi-user simulation with verifiable session-level outcomes, $μ$-Bench provides a rigorous testbed for shared voice agents.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
Artificial Intelligence.summary:
This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel detection achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.95, while vessel localisation has a median error of around 300 m for vessels longer than 100 m, and vessel AIS type-code classification achieves 62% accuracy for the majority classes. The latter, however, is highly correlated with vessel length. These results reveal both the potential and current limitations of Geospatial Foundation Models (GeoFMs) when applied to fine-grained MDA understanding in real-world scenarios.
  Additionally, a new maritime remote sensing dataset is released, pairing about 2,000 Sentinel-1 images with temporally aligned AIS signals from commercial vessels. Through manual inspection, each candidate sample was verified for bounding-box quality and for consistency between the AIS-reported vessel length and the observed vessel extent, cross-checking vessel identity and location against publicly available vessel records and, where available, photographs. The dataset was made ready for use with the NeuCo-Bench neural compression benchmark framework, publicly available on HuggingFace through https://huggingface.co/datasets/embed2scale/S1-single-ship-downstream .

Artificial Intelligence.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. However, in many large-scale annotation settings, items are annotated by different subsets of annotators. We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test), a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators. AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human annotations for each item, and substitutes one of them with an LLM annotation. This produces paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels. A replacement is supported when the inter-annotator agreement (IAA) of the mixed panel is statistically non-inferior to the IAA of the all-human panel, i.e., when the LLM preserves the signal that the human annotators share. We establish that AltRA-Test is a consistent test of asymptotic level alpha. We then evaluate it through simulations and real-world experiments in which we test 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets across text, image, audio, and video. Across these evaluations, about 100 items often suffice for the test. In simulations, where we know whether the LLM is a better or a worse annotator than the humans, AltRA-Test makes more correct replacement decisions than existing baselines. In real-world data experiments, LLMs pass the test in about half of the setups, depending mainly on the task. Since replacement is not always justified, we encourage researchers to test it for their task.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance. These strategies range from axis-parallel and oblique splits based on feature values to proximity-based splits using exemplar instances and more complex hybrid approaches. However, no single method has emerged as universally superior. In this work, we present two key contributions to the construction of greedy decision trees. First, we propose a hybrid tree architecture that integrates both feature-based and case-based splits, allowing for heterogeneous splits throughout the tree. Second, we introduce a novel type of split that leverages a selective case-based approach: when a split is needed, our method searches for the most informative subset of features to define the split, effectively balancing the specificity of case-based methods with the simplicity of feature-based ones. Experiments on a diverse set of tabular datasets show that our method outperforms standard decision trees and achieves performance on par with ensemble methods, while producing shallow trees that retain or even improve predictive accuracy.

Artificial Intelligence.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Agent patches are larger than developers', which is widely read as over-editing. But patch size does not say whether the extra edits are needed, what they are, or where they come from. We introduce Delta Residue Attribution (DRA), which replays agent trajectories, traces every block (unit) of the final patch to the step that wrote it, reverts each unit, and reruns the task tests to decide whether the unit is needed. We apply DRA to 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models on SWE-bench Verified (6,728) and DeepSWE (932), and grade developer patches using the same method. Agent patches do change more lines than developers'; on SWE-bench Verified the majority of extra edits add tests (61%) and documentation (13%) while on DeepSWE, most extra edits are code (58%). On both benchmarks, agents' code is on average at least as necessary as developers' (mean $NP_{code}$ 0.887 vs. 0.864 on SWE-bench Verified, where 11 of 18 models leave less unneeded code than developers, and 0.797 vs. 0.785 on DeepSWE). On average, 11% of an agent patch's code units on SWE-bench Verified are still unneeded, and 89% of those change behavior. Debug steps write almost none of the unneeded code. Code necessity differs substantially by model; it is unrelated to resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified and negatively correlated with it on DeepSWE (Spearman -0.59, p = 0.01). On SWE-bench Verified, pruning with DRA using only the tests the agent can see (its own tests and the repository's) removes the majority of unneeded code but also some needed code (67% recall, 46% precision), and 89% of pruned patches still resolve the task; asking the agent to audit its own diff is more precise but less effective (36% recall, 66% precision). We recommend that benchmarks report code necessity next to resolve rate and that over-editing be addressed through model training and harness-level pruning.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones. We describe and evaluate a three-way merge in which the schema defines a conflict: set algebra combines canonical triples, and a slot is contended only where a SHACL shape bounds its cardinality and both sides' changes cannot stand within that bound. Unbounded predicates union; contended slots go to a person. The same shapes graph validates the result. We do not claim the first three-way merge for RDF. Our contribution is an implementation in a production multi-agent store and an evaluation against a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge overlap rule, which it extends rather than replaces, and six other strategies. Across five synthetic seeds, the shape-aware operator raised 33 conflicts, all true positives as judged by the same shapes that define them, with no triples lost or fabricated and no SHACL violations admitted. The context-overlap baseline, counted per slot, detected the same 33 conflicts but asked 845 questions. A replay built from recorded production incidents covers 105 human alias repairs (93 after excluding 12 chained pairs) and 939 duplicate-value incidents. It reproduces a triple-level limit: different names for one entity remain invisible (0 of 93 alias repairs detected, matching 0 of 21 synthetic cases). In a study of evolving shape contracts, merging shape declarations first handles the tested cardinality changes, while datatype evolution exposes a detector blind spot caught by post-merge validation. An oracle that reads no shapes agrees with the shipped operator on the facts and history of all 23 reachable single-slot cases. Under wrong shapes, a missing bound loses data silently and a spurious one only adds questions. The supported claim is fewer human decisions with nothing silently lost, for cardinality conflicts in one deployment, not general merge correctness.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 19 pages. Artifact, benchmark and replay corpus at https://github.com/intigraph/quipu ; every table names the command that regenerates it

Artificial Intelligence.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, published in COMSNETS 2025 conference

Artificial Intelligence.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Since vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, accelerating these demonstrations before fine-tuning can lead to faster VLA policies without an additional speed-selection module at deployment. Several offline speedup methods have focused on identifying segments that require less precision and assigning predefined speedup factors to the segments. However, even within a single segment, a speedup factor suitable for steady motion may be too high when precise alignment is required. To this end, this paper presents RePace, an offline reasoning framework that determines how much to accelerate each part of a demonstration. For the same recorded movement, RePace measures how much each candidate speedup factor shortens the sequence and compares the resulting observation-action pairs used for training. Given the task instruction, a pretrained language model uses the visual context and original motion of successive windows to interpret these candidate retiming effects and select a speedup profile for the complete episode. Experimental results demonstrate that RePace outperforms the baselines in overall task execution efficiency on both LIBERO and RoboCasa-Kitchen. On all three tasks with a gripper-equipped Franka Research 3 arm, RePace matches or exceeds the acceleration baselines in success rate and completes successful trials faster.

Artificial Intelligence.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
Artificial Intelligence.summary: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets. We pair images from these datasets with VLM-generated and human-verified referring expressions, and derive accurate ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes of the referred objects from their 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Our systematic evaluation of 17 frontier VLMs across the major proprietary and open-weight families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen, Gemma) shows that the best model, Gemini 4 Carbon, reaches 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D, despite the more lenient IoU thresholds in 3D. The predicted 3D boxes are usually centered on the target objects in the image but often off in depth by more than the object's size, suggesting that metric scale estimation, which needs reliable object size priors, is currently by far the main source of error.

Artificial Intelligence.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix. We ask whether fine-tuning the model to the decision objective can do better. We fine-tune the same pretrained model so that its restricted softmax over label tokens (already a distribution over business actions) maximizes expected utility under an institution-specified, amount-scaled cost matrix. Because the reward is a known function of (action, outcome, amount) and the outcome is observed in the data, the expected-utility objective and its gradient are available in closed form. This is example-dependent cost-sensitive learning whose per-example loss is linear in the predicted probability, with no sampling, critics, or advantage estimation. A KL anchor to the pretrained model and an auxiliary language-modeling term preserve calibration and the generative event model. A sampled, group-normalized (GRPO-style) variant provides the extension point to trajectory-level rewards.

Artificial Intelligence.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related knowledge chains, with their geometric mean giving overall coverage. The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. Evaluating 16 deep research agents reveals different strengths in breadth and depth, with the best-performing agent reaching 57.04% overall coverage. Rubric judgments agree closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across the tested metric configurations.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Network of Theseus (like the ship)
Artificial Intelligence.summary: A standard assumption in deep learning is that the inductive bias introduced by a neural network architecture must persist from training through inference. The architecture you train with is the architecture you deploy. This assumption constrains the community from selecting architectures that may have desirable efficiency or design properties due to difficulties with optimization. We challenge this assumption with the Network of Theseus (NoT), a method for progressively converting a trained, or even untrained, guide network architecture part-by-part into an entirely different target network architecture while preserving the performance of the guide network. At each stage, components in the guide network architecture are incrementally replaced with the target architecture modules and aligned via representational similarity metrics. This procedure preserves most of the functionality of the guide network even under substantial architectural changes-for example, converting a convolutional network into a multilayer perceptron, or GPT-2 into a recurrent neural network. By decoupling optimization from deployment, NoT expands the space of viable inference-time architectures, opening opportunities for better accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs and enabling more directed exploration of the architectural design space.

Artificial Intelligence.title: Frozen Factor or Spectral Band? In LoRA, the Factor Matters More at Low Rank
Artificial Intelligence.summary: On two main task-model pairs, at ranks 1 to 8 with few optimiser steps, the factor a LoRA variant freezes matters more than its band of singular directions. MiCA and PiCa are compared by band, minor against dominant, yet MiCA freezes the output factor B and PiCa, in our notation, the input factor A. We cross factor and band in a 2 x 2 design on models from 1B to 8B parameters. Freezing A beats freezing B on both bands, by +12 to +20 points at rank 2 on a format task, our primary evidence, and still by about +7 points at rank 8 on OpenBookQA. A Holm correction over 258 primary tests, added post hoc, keeps this advantage in 15 of 16 tests and the lead of factor over band at ranks 1, 2 and 4, rank 1 of the format task being itself post hoc. At rank 8 that lead passes its own test but not the correction. The advantage repeats at rank 2 with two 7B models, by +11 to +13 points. Outside the correction, it repeats on GSM8K with a 1B model and, in a post hoc experiment, with an 8B model at ranks 8 and 16. It holds when B frozen gets as many parameters or more, with a random frozen A, and with sixteen times the format-task budget. It narrows above rank 8 on most pairs, at rank 8 with the 8B model on the two main tasks, on ARC and in a task mixture, and it closes at the last step of longer training on OpenBookQA. At MiCA's and PiCa's own settings, it is smaller or not detected.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: v2: rewritten; crossed factor-by-band design with pre-specified tests; eight seeds; ranks 1 to 64; 7B and 8B models; GSM8K. 42 pages

Artificial Intelligence.title: AI Lifecycle-Aware Feasibility Framework for Split-RIC Orchestration in NTN O-RAN
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) is constrained by the joint limits of satellite Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP), feeder-link capacity, and orbital connectivity, which directly affect O-RAN closed-loop control and AI lifecycle management. This paper studies the feasibility of distributing the O-RAN intelligence across Ground, LEO, and GEO segments through three representative deployments: (i) Ground-Centric control with telemetry streaming, (ii) a ground-LEO Split-RIC with on-board inference and store-and-forward model refresh, and (iii) GEO-LEO multi-layer control enabled by inter-satellite links. For each deployment, we derive closed-form expressions for lifecycle energy, near-real-time control latency, and model-refresh latency, while explicitly enforcing power-feasible spaceborne computational throughput. Pairwise analytical boundaries and numerical sensitivity analysis over telemetry volume, feeder-link conditions, inference workload, model longevity, and orbital waiting time identify the operating regions in which different placements are energetically preferable or satisfy model-refresh requirements. The results show that the architecture choice is inherently lifecycle- and constraint-dependent, providing decision-enabling primitives for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) level AI placement and lifecycle orchestration in NTN O-RAN.
Artificial Intelligence.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures. Major revision following peer review: corrected power-feasible computation, energy and latency models, numerical results, and feasibility boundaries. Revised manuscript submitted to IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

Artificial Intelligence.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality. Whether their outputs still carry model-specific characteristics matters for attribution, for model comparison beyond aggregate quality, and for evaluations that assume anonymity. We ask whether images from frontier T2I models can still be classified by source, and which visual properties make this possible. Here we show that a standard ResNet-50 identifies the source of an image among HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, the four highest-ranked open-source models on the Text-to-Image Arena, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts. Human participants reach only 62.61% on the pairwise version of this task, so the distinguishing cues are not visually obvious. They are also not tied to a particular classifier and survive severe image corruptions and out-of-distribution prompts. We trace them to visual idiosyncrasies at three levels. Low-level texture statistics alone let a lightweight multi-layer perceptron match ResNet-50. Object layout, depth, and albedo estimated from the images each carry a source signal. Image captions reveal model-specific preferences in style and background that the prompts never specify. A one-sentence hint about these cues raises human accuracy by 9.03 percentage points. These idiosyncrasies make source classification a tool for measuring similarity between models and between real and generated images, and they caution against assuming anonymity in human preference evaluation of T2I models.

Artificial Intelligence.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
Artificial Intelligence.summary: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at $4\times10^9$ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. We present an artificial neural network model that maps the unordered multi-set of molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio $I(t)/I_0$ in 1-3 milliseconds. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Each constituent is embedded with a chemistry-pretrained transformer language model, ChemBERTa. In our proposed method, training data are produced by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using the radiation source at 30, 80, 100, and 120 kV tube voltages over polyethylene-based shielding composite slabs of thicknesses spanning 0.15-2.5 mm.
